```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Figure references

## Directly produce in a qmd file
See @fig-1.
```{r}
#| label: fig-1
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of weight"

# hist(mtcars$wt)
 
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.3)
# ggsave(file = "z_fig-wthist.png")
```

## Embed a png image

You may use the knitr function `knitr::include_graphics()`. This is particularly useful when your code is very long.

```json
#| label: fig-3
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of weight"
knitr::include_graphics("z_fig-wthist.png")
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-2
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of weight"

knitr::include_graphics("z_fig-wthist.png")
```

Now, using the code below, control the size of the figure.

```json
#| out.width: "80%"
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-3
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of weight"
#| out.width: "80%"
#| out.height: "30%"

knitr::include_graphics("z_fig-wthist.png")
```
